q41.question: Under the Trade Credit Insurance policy, a Counterparty becomes insolvent. Within what period must the Insured submit a complete claim, and from which date does that period run?
q41.ground_truth: Within 60 days after the Date of Loss. For a loss due to Insolvency, the Date of Loss is the Due Date, which is the payment date originally set by the Contract.

q42.question: Under the Trade Credit Insurance policy, the Insured's payments record with a Counterparty for the recent one year is INR 1,000 million. What is the highest Preliminary limit the Insured may set, and for how long may it be applied if the Insurer has not yet determined a Credit limit?
q42.ground_truth: INR 200 million. One quarter of the payments record is INR 250 million, but the Preliminary limit cannot exceed INR 200 million. It may be applied for 3 months from the date it was set up, unless the Insurer restricts it.

q42.answer:
Under the Trade Credit Insurance policy, the Insured may establish up to 1/4 of the aggregate payments record of the recent one (1) year with a Counterparty as the Preliminary limit, but the Preliminary limit of such Counterparty does not exceed INR 200 million.

1/4 of INR 1,000 million = INR 250 million, but this is capped at INR 200 million. Therefore, the highest Preliminary limit the Insured may set is INR 200 million.

If the Credit Limit has not yet been determined, the Preliminary limit may be applied for 3 (three) months from the date of setting up the Preliminary limit.

Under the Auto Secure Commercial Vehicle Package Policy, for partial losses (losses other than Total Loss/Constructive Total Loss), the Company pays the actual and reasonable costs of repair and/or replacement of parts lost/damaged **subject to depreciation as per limits specified**. However, no depreciation shall be deducted on Non-OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer)/Non-OES (Original Equipment Supplier) parts used in repairs. Also, deductions on account of depreciation on the parts admissible under the depreciation reimbursement cover will not be applicable if the depreciation reimbursement cover is also opted and shown in the policy schedule.

Under the Contractors Plant and Machinery Insurance policy, where damage to an insured item can be repaired, the Company pays expenses necessarily incurred to restore the damaged machine to its condition immediately prior to the accident/loss. **No deduction shall be made for depreciation in respect of parts replaced, except those with limited life**, but the value of any salvage will be taken into account.

"Third Party" means any natural person and/or legal person and/or association of persons except You and Your Family Members. Since the 20-year-old child is not within the definition of "You" or "Your Family Members," they would be treated as a Third Party.

q81.answer:
Under the **Auto Secure Commercial Vehicle Package Policy**, a damaged item is settled as a total loss when the cost of repair is equal to or exceeds the value of the damaged item immediately before the event; in that case, the market value of the item as it existed immediately before the occurrence of the loss is paid, less salvage value.

Under the **Port Package policy (handling equipment)**, a Constructive Total Loss (CTL) applies if the reasonable costs of repair of damage sustained in one accident are estimated to exceed the insured value; the insured value is then paid as a CTL, less any salvage value.

Under the **Contractors Plant and Machinery Insurance policy**, where an insured item is totally destroyed, the Company will pay the actual value of the item immediately before the occurrence of the loss, including costs for ordinary freight, erection and customs duties if any, provided such expenses have been included in the sum insured, such actual value to be calculated by deducting proper depreciation from the replacement value of the item.

q86.question: What happens to the insurance when the insured property is sold or changes owner under the Auto Secure Commercial Vehicle Package Policy, the SBI General Livestock policy, and the Bharat Griha Raksha policy?
q86.ground_truth: Auto Secure: the Liability Only cover is deemed transferred to the new owner from the date of transfer, and the transferee must apply within 14 days. SBI General Livestock: the policy stands cancelled and no payment is made if ownership of the animal passes to another person, except by operation of law. Bharat Griha Raksha: the policy ends when the insured sells or releases the interest in the home building or contents.

q104.ground_truth: No, unless the Insurer has agreed otherwise in writing. A blood relationship between directors of the Insured and the Counterparty, up to direct cousins, is a Controlling influence. The Insurer has no liability for losses where a Controlling influence can arise between the Insured and the Counterparty.

q114.question: A crane at our container terminal is insured for less than it is worth on the market. When does the insurer scale down a damage payout, and when does it not?
q114.ground_truth: The reduction (Average) applies only if the insured value is less than 80% of the market value of the item. The payout is then reduced by the percentage by which the insured value is below the market value. It does not apply if the insured value is an agreed value, and it does not apply to freight charges and labour costs.

q114.answer:
The insurer scales down a damage payout under the Average provision. According to the context, if the market value of an item of equipment at the time of an accident is greater than the insured value, the insurer will reduce reimbursement by the percentage by which the insured value of the item is less than the market value.

This scaling down applies only if the insured value is less than 80% of the market value of the item, and it applies separately to each item of equipment.

It does **not** apply:
- to freight charges and labour costs
- if the insured value is an agreed value

Also, the Average provision does not require the insurer to pay more than the insured value for any item of equipment.

q120.question: My house fell down by itself, not because of fire, flood or any other listed event. Does my home cover continue?
q120.ground_truth: No. The policy ends automatically 7 days after the home building collapses or is destroyed by a reason other than an Insured Event. The insured can apply within 7 days to continue the cover, but the insurer is not bound to agree.
